newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile court backs U.S. surgeons in operations row.
newsitem.headline: Chile court backs U.S. surgeons in operations row.

text.p: A Chilean court on Thursday rejected a legal bid by local doctors to stop a team of U.S plastic surgeons from operating on children with facial deformities at a Chilean hospital.

The U.S. medical team, which came to Chile under Rotary International's Rotaplast 97 programme, had temporarily suspended operations earlier this week after the legal dispute over the treatment blew up.
"This decision means that the Rotaplast programme will be able to continue carrying out the surgical operations planned at the Gustave Fricke hospital," Health Minister Alex Figueroa said.
The doctors were planning to operate on around 100 children from poor families suffering from disfiguring hair-lips and cleft-palates at the state-run hospital in the seaside resort of Vina del Mar.

The Medical College that brought the lawsuit accused the 28-strong team of "illegally exercising their profession" in Chile and claiming they were carrying out experimental operations with poor children.
The college's move caused indignation in the press and has been heavily criticised by other doctors who have accused it of taking an attitude of "excessive professional jealousy."

The U.S team suspended operations on Tuesday because of the legal wrangle, but then restarted them after receiving written assurances from the Health Ministry that they would not face criminal charges.
The medical team, who are all volunteers, came to Chile during their vacations and brought their own equipment, Anita Stangle, head of the Rotaplast programme, said.
